# Commands

Inspect the window with `canopy ls` and `canopy status`.
`canopy commands` lists the app actions below, even without an open window.

Run an action in the open window with `canopy do`:

```sh
canopy do pane.split --direction right
canopy do pane.split '{"direction":"right"}'
```

Arguments can be named flags or one JSON object. Required arguments are marked below.
Actions use the current selection unless you give an explicit target.
Some actions close terminals; read their descriptions before running them.
Mods can add their own actions, which are not listed here.

## `canvas.zoom_in`

Zoom the canvas in one step.

No arguments.

## `canvas.zoom_out`

Zoom the canvas out one step.

No arguments.

## `canvas.zoom_reset`

Reset canvas zoom.

No arguments.

## `canvas.arrange`

Arrange selected cells or the current space: tidy, row, column or wires. Omit layout to repeat the last; picker opens the layout menu.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `layout` | no |
| `picker` | no |
| `space` | no |

## `canvas.undo`

Restore geometry before the last canvas move, resize or arrange.

No arguments.

## `canvas.tile`

Tile view: fit every expanded terminal and agent of the current space into the visible canvas, tmux-style, with the selected one largest; collapsed ones line up below. Other panes stay where they are. Repeat to put everything back.

No arguments.

## `canvas.fit`

Fit the selection, else everything in the current space or Home; repeat to restore the previous camera.

No arguments.

## `canvas.mode`

Enter canvas mode: its keys take priority and unbound keys are swallowed until Enter or Escape.

No arguments.

## `canvas.leave`

Cancel a keyboard connection, or leave canvas mode with selection unchanged.

No arguments.

## `canvas.enter`

Complete a keyboard connection, or expand the selected cell and leave canvas mode.

No arguments.

## `canvas.go`

Select the nearest shown cell left, right, up or down without expanding it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `canvas.space`

Go into the next or prev space, space N (1-based, top strip order) or a space id, or the recent / oldest one entered; its cells fill the canvas.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `canvas.home`

Leave the space for Home: space cards and cells outside any space.

No arguments.

## `canvas.select_all`

Select every terminal and agent cell in the current place; only with canvas focus, so an entered terminal keeps its own select-all.

No arguments.

## `canvas.fit_all`

Fit everything in the current place, whatever is selected; repeat to restore the previous camera.

No arguments.

## `canvas.collapse`

Collapse the selected terminal cell.

No arguments.

## `canvas.connect`

Start a keyboard connection from the selected cell; move to the other cell and press Enter.

No arguments.

## `canvas.nudge`

Move the selected cell left, right, up or down by one canvas gap, with one undo step.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `canvas.new`

Create a terminal beside the selected cell, in its space. With like: true, start what the selected cell runs (an agent or other startable program), else a plain terminal.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `like` | no |

## `canvas.agents`

Open the installed agent list beside the selected cell.

No arguments.

## `quote.menu`

Open the quote popover at point or the pointer: agents wired to the quoted pane first, then other running agents, then installed agents to start with the quote.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `path` | yes |
| `start` | no |
| `end` | no |
| `text` | yes |
| `point` | no |
| `pane` | no |
| `kind` | no |
| `source` | no |

## `canvas.close_focused`

Close the focused Files panel tab, or the one selected canvas pane. A browser closes its active tab, and its last tab closes the pane; with several or no panes selected, nothing closes. Only the person can run it.

No arguments.

## `canvas.close`

Close every selected pane (else the focused one) behind one dialog listing them, the named terminal, or one file or mod pane by id (pane; a mod pane holding text refuses); terminals and panes are the confirmed lists, closed without asking; working sub-agents refuse. Dialogs pass confirmed as agent or terminal, and dont_ask disables future plain-terminal prompts.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `terminals` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |
| `dont_ask` | no |
| `pane` | no |
| `panes` | no |

## `canvas.note_new`

Open a sticky note on the canvas. The optional point is in world coordinates.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `point` | no |

## `canvas.pane_new`

Open a file, browser, sim (on a Mac with Xcode), or mod:<name> pane. Files require path. A browser accepts an HTTP(S) address, an absolute local path or a file URL, and opens New tab when url is omitted. A sim opens udid (a simulator or "booted") or lists devices to pick; with udid, url (http(s) or an app link) opens on it once booted, and the reply waits for the device: name, runtime, state and url, or a screenshot path when no url was opened (read the pane to see the page). place is "panel" (a tab in the Files panel, the default for browsers and sims), "canvas" (at point, the middle of the view by default) or "pinned" (the top right of the screen; pinned: true is the same). Pass wire to place it beside a terminal and wire it in that terminal's space. A file path already open moves its pane. The reply includes pane, kind, wired and the pane's path or url when applicable; for a browser with a url it waits until the page has loaded and adds title. `canopy pane new` puts browsers and sims on the canvas unless place says otherwise.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `kind` | yes |
| `path` | no |
| `url` | no |
| `udid` | no |
| `wire` | no |
| `point` | no |
| `place` | no |
| `pinned` | no |

## `canvas.pane_dock`

Dock a browser or sim pane as a tab in the Files panel, or with docked false move it back onto the canvas at its saved place. Without docked it toggles. Acts on pane, else the selected pane. Replies with pane and docked.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `docked` | no |

## `canvas.pane_pin`

Pin a pane where it shows on screen, so it stays there while the canvas pans and zooms, or with pinned false move it back onto the canvas. Without pinned it toggles. Acts on pane, else the selected pane. Replies with pane and pinned.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `pinned` | no |

## `canvas.pane_set`

Merge props (an object) into a mod pane's saved props; mods save their state with it, and a string props.text is what canopy pane read returns. Replies with nothing.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | yes |
| `props` | yes |

## `canvas.hand`

Hand tool: while on, a left drag anywhere on the canvas pans, as with Space held. Without on it toggles.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `on` | no |

## `canvas.pane_read`

A pane's text inside a <pane-content> envelope that marks it as untrusted, cut at 256 KiB. Replies with text.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | yes |

## `canvas.pane_shot`

Save a pane as drawn on screen to a PNG (default: <temp>/canopy/<pane>.png); refuses when it is off screen. Replies with path.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | yes |
| `path` | no |

## `canvas.pane_open`

Point a browser or simulator pane at a target. A browser loads an HTTP(S) address, an absolute local path or a file URL in its active tab and makes it Home. Pass tab: new to open the URL in a new browser tab. A bare localhost:3000 uses http. Open URL without a target focuses the address field when a browser pane is given or selected. A sim takes a udid or "booted" (refreshing the screenshot when already showing that device) or a URL to open on its device, booting it first; the reply waits for the device and includes name, runtime, state and url, or a screenshot path when no url was opened. A browser reply waits until the page has loaded and adds title.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | yes |
| `target` | yes |
| `tab` | no |

## `canvas.browser_tab_new`

Open a new tab in a browser pane. Pass an HTTP(S) address, an absolute local path or a file URL, or omit url for an empty tab. Replies with pane and tab. With no pane and no single browser pane selected, runs canvas.new.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `url` | no |

## `canvas.browser_tab_close`

Close a tab in a browser pane. Without tab, closes the active tab. Closing the last tab closes the pane. With no pane and no single browser pane selected, runs tab.close if bound.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `tab` | no |

Focus a pane (or the pane showing a terminal); a file, browser or other canvas pane is selected and brought into view.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `pane.go`

Focus the pane or focusable mod to the "left", "right", "up" or "down".

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `pane.swap`

Swap a pane (default: the focused one) with its neighbor in a direction, or with another pane of its tab (target). Give exactly one of direction or target.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | no |
| `pane` | no |
| `target` | no |

## `terminal.peek`

Peek at a running terminal over the tab, with keep-as-tab and close controls.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `terminal.show`

Show a terminal in a pane for now, in place of its own (no terminal: back).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `pane` | no |

## `terminal.select_all`

Select a terminal's whole screen and scrollback (default: the focused one), ready to copy. On the alternate screen, select only that screen.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.copy`

Copy the focused terminal's selection. With nothing selected, that key goes to the program.

No arguments.

## `terminal.scroll`

Scroll a terminal's view of its history (default: the focused one). Give exactly one of: lines (a whole number; negative goes up, toward history), pages (a number, fractions allowed; one page is the terminal's rows), to: "top" (oldest history) or "bottom" (the live screen). This scrolls Canopy's view, not the program.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `lines` | no |
| `pages` | no |
| `to` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.paste`

Paste into the focused terminal (copied files as if dropped; an image alone as terminal.paste_image pastes it).

No arguments.

## `terminal.paste_image`

Ctrl+V: the clipboard's image as a file on the focused terminal's machine, when that's another one; on Windows, paste clipboard text; otherwise Ctrl+V goes to the terminal.

No arguments.

## `terminal.search`

Search the focused terminal's screen and scrollback; the find bar and query stay with that terminal.

No arguments.

## `agent.focus`

Show an agent (sub-agents too). On the canvas it also enters its pane.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `agent.next`

Show the next agent, in the order the agents list shows them.

No arguments.

## `agent.prev`

Show the previous agent.

No arguments.

## `layout.switch`

Show a layout (layouts/<name>.json), or the next one.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |

## `layout.clone`

Duplicate a layout as <name>-copy (or as), then show it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | yes |
| `as` | no |

## `mod.clone`

Duplicate a mod as <name>-copy (or as).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | yes |
| `as` | no |

## `layout.set`

Replace a personal layout tree; shipped layouts accept only click/look fields (not structure).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `layout` | yes |

## `layout.toggle`

Hide or show a layout node.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |

## `layout.show`

Show a layout node.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |

## `layout.hide`

Hide a layout node.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |

## `layout.resize`

Size a layout node.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |
| `px` | no |
| `weight` | no |

## `layout.select`

Show one child of a stack.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `stack` | yes |
| `child` | yes |

## `layout.reset`

Reset a shipped layout and its clicks (the old file is kept aside).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |

## `mod.open`

Toggle a mod as the overlay its mod.json describes; calling again closes it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | yes |

## `overlay.close`

Close an overlay (default: the top dialog or popup).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |

## `app.help`

Toggle the keys dialog.

No arguments.

## `app.welcome`

Show the welcome again.

No arguments.

## `app.palette`

Toggle the command palette: every command by name, with its key; calling again closes it.

No arguments.

## `app.settings`

Open the settings (section: look, keyboard, shortcuts, alerts).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `section` | no |

## `app.reset`

The escape hatch: set the shown layout and keys aside, back to the default screen.

No arguments.

## `app.theme`

Use a theme (a preset or themes/<name>.json).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | yes |

## `app.zoom_in`

Make everything bigger.

No arguments.

## `app.zoom_out`

Make everything smaller.

No arguments.

## `app.zoom_reset`

Back to normal size.

No arguments.

## `app.menu`

Open the shared primary command menu, optionally a named group.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `group` | no |

## `app.quit`

Quit Canopy. Terminals keep running in the core.

No arguments.

## `app.hide`

Hide the app (macOS).

No arguments.

## `app.hide_others`

Hide other apps (macOS).

No arguments.

## `app.show_all`

Show all apps (macOS).

No arguments.

## `window.close`

Close the window (on Linux, quits).

No arguments.

## `window.minimize`

Minimize the window.

No arguments.

## `window.maximize`

Maximize the window, or back.

No arguments.

## `canvas.pane_quote`

Open the quote menu for the last selected image pane.

No arguments.

## `canvas.pdf_find`

Toggle text search in the last selected PDF pane.

No arguments.

## `canvas.pdf_highlight`

Toggle text highlight mode in the last selected PDF pane.

No arguments.

## `canvas.pdf_prev`

Go to the previous page in the last selected PDF pane.

No arguments.

## `canvas.pdf_next`

Go to the next page in the last selected PDF pane.

No arguments.

|---|---|
| `from` | yes |
| `to` | no |

| `to` | no |
| `into` | no |

|---|---|

|---|---|
